population.definition: Département de Dakar (the core city: its 79 km2 area, without Pikine, Guédiawaye, Keur Massar or Rufisque); the wider Dakar region counted 4,004,426 inhabitants

facts.claim: Before the French arrived, the Cape Verde peninsula, where Dakar stands, had been occupied by the Lebu people since the end of the 14th century.

source.title: Dakar, Portrait of a Capital City (review)
source.quote: the Dakar peninsula was occupied by the Lebu people from the end of the 14th century

facts.claim: In 1857 a French ship's captain, Protêt, took possession of Dakar and on 25 May declared the place a French possession.

source.title: Dakar, a French town in May 1857
source.quote: He transformed this house into a fortress and then on 25 May declared the place a French possession

facts.claim: Colonists began moving from over-populated Gorée to the fishing village of Dakar, which had a natural deep port.

source.title: Dakar, a French town in May 1857
source.quote: When Gorea became over populated, colonists began moving to the nearby fishing village of Dakar with its natural deep port

facts.claim: In 1902 the capital of French West Africa moved from Saint-Louis to Dakar.

source.title: Dakar, Portrait of a Capital City (review)
source.quote: In 1902, the capital of French West Africa (Afrique de l’Ouest Française, AOF) moved from Saint‑Louis to Dakar

facts.claim: Dakar's population rose from 3,000 in 1869 to 18,000 in 1904 and 214,000 in 1945.

source.title: Dakar, Portrait of a Capital City (review)
source.quote: The population increased from 3,000 in 1869 to 18,000 in 1904, 34,000 in 1926, 92,000 in 1936, and 214,000 in 1945

facts.claim: The Dakar region lies at the extreme west of the Cap-Vert peninsula, on the Atlantic coast, and covers about 550 km2.

source.title: RGPH-5 Région de Dakar : rapport de présentation des résultats
source.publisher: ANSD (Agence nationale de la Statistique et de la Démographie)
source.quote: La région de Dakar est située à l’extrême ouest de la presqu’île du Cap-Vert, tout au bord de l’océan atlantique et s’étend sur une superficie de 550 km²

facts.claim: Since June 1958 the Dakar region has been the seat of government and the capital of the country.

source.title: RGPH-5 Région de Dakar : rapport de présentation des résultats
source.publisher: ANSD (Agence nationale de la Statistique et de la Démographie)
source.quote: Depuis juin 1958, la région de Dakar est devenue le siège du Gouvernement en étant la capitale du pays

facts.claim: The Pointe des Almadies, at the north-west of the Cap-Vert peninsula, is the westernmost point of the African continent.

source.title: Pointe des Almadies
source.quote: It is the westernmost point of the continent africain

facts.claim: The Port of Dakar handled 29.66 million tonnes of traffic in 2025, up from 24.58 million tonnes the year before.

facts.claim: In the Dakar region 68.7% of residents aged 3 and over often use Wolof.

source.publisher: Biennale de l'art africain contemporain de Dakar
source.quote: Instituée en 1989 avec une première édition en 1990 consacrée à la littérature. Celle de 1992 est la première consacrée aux arts plastiques

facts.claim: The Dakar Biennale's 1996 edition began a series reserved exclusively for the visual arts of Africa and its diaspora.

source.title: Histoire de la Biennale de Dakar

places.name: Island of Gorée
places.what: Gorée is a small island less than four kilometres off the coast of Dakar. It was inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List in 1978 and has become the emblem of the transatlantic slave trade, although the island's central role in that trade is now debated.

places.what: A 49-metre bronze statue in Dakar, unveiled on 3 April 2010 and meant to symbolise the triumph of African liberation. Some sources give a different height of 52 metres.

places.name: Musée des Civilisations Noires
places.what: A national museum in Dakar covering 14,000 m2 and designed to hold 18,000 pieces, from the first hominids to contemporary art. The idea was launched by Senghor in 1966 and the museum was inaugurated in 2018.

source.quote: D'une surface de 14.000 m2, il pourra accueillir 18.000 pièces

source.title: Sénégal: inauguration du Musée des civilisations noires à Dakar (AFP)

places.name: Marché Sandaga
places.what: A great hall built in the Sudanese-Sahel tradition in 1933, which for almost a century was one of Dakar's main trading centres. Demolition began in August 2020.

source.title: Excavation begins at historic Dakar market in renovation project (AFP)
source.quote: The great hall, built in the Sudanese-Sahel tradition in 1933, has housed hundreds of stalls selling merchandise of all kinds

myth.claim: Gorée is often presented as the centre of the transatlantic slave trade.
myth.truth: UNESCO's own Courier notes that the central role of the island in the history of the transatlantic slave trade is now debated, even though its House of Slaves became the emblem of that history.

source.title: Gorée island, destination for memorial tourism
source.quote: even if the central role of the island in the history of the transatlantic slave trade is now debated

notNotFound: UNESCO World Heritage Centre pages (whc.unesco.org) return 403, so Gorée facts rely on the UNESCO Courier and the UN Africa Renewal.
Monument height: sources give 49 m (Africanews), 50 m and 52 m (Politis); recorded as disputed.
MCN exact inauguration date (6 December 2018 in other press) not verified in a readable page; only the year is recorded.
City-proper census figure is for the département de Dakar; the commune d'arrondissement boundaries differ.
Sandaga year of opening beyond 1933 and Dakar independence 1960 date not verified from a readable non-excluded source.
